86d6bfdad1: Air flows past the vocal folds, and the vocal tract shapes the sound
53d88d7175: Challenge: arrange the seven links in order, "from breathing to sound".

e771820153: If any link tenses up, the whole path suffers. Singing and speaking both come from the voice, but singing covers a wider range, lasts longer and relies more on a steady supply of breath.

83554929bf: Build4. Caring for your voice
e2beddf776: Myth or fact? Guess with a show of hands, then flip the card
52f95161c5: When your throat is dry, iced water feels best
e708c1a4ca: MythIced water makes the throat muscles tighten; warm water keeps the vocal folds moist.
05904afdd9: Whispering lets your vocal folds rest
f39d641a91: MythWhispering actually tenses the vocal folds; the real rest is to stop talking.
ba667c7f4d: Drinking milk before singing soothes the throat
8f90b54466: MythMilk and chocolate tend to cause phlegm; avoid them for three hours before performing.
850d8856dc: Drink 1,500 to 2,000 ml of warm water a day
229d886c1a: FactMoist membranes let the vocal folds vibrate freely; drink a little at a time, often.
eb89748767: When your throat feels stuck, give a hard cough
9bf685fae3: MythSwallow instead; a hard cough slams the vocal folds together.
8aadcc9d33: Being hoarse the day after karaoke is normal, so just ignore it
150dea79b0: MythYou need rest and water. If hoarseness lasts more than two weeks, see an ENT doctor.
899a61dc49: A drink now and then is fine, even around a performance
e521b23d13: MythAlcohol makes the vocal folds swell with blood; avoid it before and after singing.
3d361e17e7: Pause intense practice when you have a cold
c50975ff7b: FactForcing yourself to sing with swollen vocal folds is the easiest way to get hurt.

ae057236cc: Singing breath rests on the lower belly muscles. It goes by many names: dantian breathing, diaphragmatic breathing, belly breathing. The point is always chest and belly working together.

ba80b88f41: The waist expands at the front, sides and back
c31dbd4439: Breathing in, the waist expands all the way round while shoulders and collarbones stay still; breathing out, the waist and belly slowly draw back in.

a2de8daeb7:
When the /s/ exhale runs out, press lightly on your belly with your hand, then breathe in quickly.
Breathing out on /i/ instead also trains the belly muscles.
309b18313e:
After a full breath, hold it and count, then breathe out.
Count a little longer each time.

9282d39761: When you're short of breath, line endings go weak and drag, and you may even break in the middle of a word. Mark your breath points first, then sing.
